analysis.one_liner: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Limited (VAML) runs India's largest integrated aluminium business - the Lanjigarh alumina refinery, the giant Jharsuguda smelter, and a 51% stake in BALCO - after being demerged out of Vedanta Ltd and listed separately in June 2026.
analysis.whats_happening: On 18 Sep 2026 VAML disclosed that effectively all of its promoter group's shareholding (99.99%) is encumbered against financing facilities - a significant disclosure for a company listed barely three months earlier. On 3 Oct 2026 it reported record Q2 FY27 production (aluminium 649 KT, +5% YoY; alumina 895 KT, +37% YoY), but the Q2 financial results themselves have not yet been released and no confirmed date is available - check BSE/NSE filings. The stock touched a post-listing low of ₹359.55-366.85 in mid-October before closing at ₹371.85 on 16 Oct 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: VAML is a brand-new standalone listing - it was carved out of Vedanta Ltd and only started trading on its own in June 2026, so there is no multi-year track record to judge it by yet. The business itself (bauxite-to-alumina-to-aluminium, plus part-ownership of BALCO) reported strong first-quarter profits, but the stock has fallen about 24% since listing and almost all the promoter's shares are pledged. The tension is this: operationally the numbers look good, but a heavily leveraged/pledged promoter holding and a falling share price in the same few months is not a comfortable combination for new shareholders.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June quarter, VAML's first standalone results, announced 30 Jul 2026): revenue ₹21,393 Cr (+46% YoY), EBITDA ₹10,299 Cr (+135% YoY, ~48% margin), PAT ₹6,597 Cr (+205% YoY), EPS ₹14.39. Management attributed the jump to record volumes and favourable LME aluminium/alumina spreads. Because this is the company's first quarter as a standalone demerged entity, the YoY comparison is against carve-out/pro-forma numbers from when VAML was part of Vedanta Ltd, not a like-for-like standalone prior year - treat the growth percentages as directionally useful but not strictly comparable. Q2 FY27 (Sept quarter): only production data is out so far (record aluminium and alumina output, filed 3 Oct 2026); financial results (revenue/EBITDA/PAT) have not been published - Not verified, check Screener/BSE for the actual release date.
analysis.performance_read: VAML has been listed for only about four months (since 15 Jun 2026), so there is no genuine long-term return history to assess - short_history_mode applies and any '1-year' or 'all-time' figure here is really just this same four-month window. In that window the stock has fallen from a peak of ₹487.42 to ₹371.85, a 23.7% drawdown, and has underperformed both the Nifty (-4.9% to -9.5% over the same periods) and peer Hindalco (which was up 17% over one year) across every horizon measured. There is no corporate-action price adjustment needed here (no splits, and the demerger pricing is already reflected in the start of this series) - the decline is a straight market re-rating since listing, not a chart artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 9x, VAML looks statistically cheap for a company posting ~48% EBITDA margins. But why it looks cheap matters more than whether it is cheap: aluminium is a cyclical, LME-price-linked commodity business, VAML has no standalone earnings history to extrapolate from, and the 99.99% promoter pledge creates an ownership overhang that markets typically discount for. Clean ROE/ROCE figures could not be verified - some data sources show 0% (almost certainly a data artifact from the company's newness as a listed entity rather than a true reflection of returns) - Not verified, check on Screener once a full trailing-twelve-month standalone history exists.
analysis.growth_read: Both margin and volume moved up together in Q1 FY27 - EBITDA margin expanded sharply alongside a 46% revenue increase, and the Q2 production update (aluminium +5% YoY, alumina +37% YoY) shows volumes still rising. This is not a case of flat volumes propped up by margin alone; however, since aluminium/alumina prices are LME-linked and currently favourable, a chunk of the margin gain is cyclical rather than purely operational, and that is worth separating out once more standalone quarters are available.
analysis.health_read: Whether Q1's strong EBITDA converted into free cash flow could not be verified from available sources - Not verified, check on Screener. Debt-to-equity is reported by some trackers as negative (implying a net cash position), but this conflicts with the unreliable ROE/ROCE figures from the same sources, so the clean balance-sheet picture is not yet verifiable. The more concrete and immediate risk is not VAML's own business economics (which look healthy on reported margins) but an ownership/financing-structure risk: the promoter group has pledged virtually all of its stake, which is a red flag around parent-level leverage rather than the operating company's own health.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold about 56.4% of VAML, entirely through foreign Vedanta entities (Twin Star Holdings ~40%, Vedanta Holdings Mauritius II ~12.6%, Vedanta Holdings Mauritius ~2.75%) - there is no Indian promoter entity on the register. As of 18 Sep 2026, 99.99% of this promoter shareholding was disclosed as encumbered against financing facilities, which is a significant governance watchpoint for a newly listed company. Institutional holding is roughly 11% FII and 15% DII, with ~17% public float; the government holds a residual 0.07% stake (left over from the demerger structure). No well-known individual investor or marquee fund was found to hold a notable stake - Not verified beyond the institutional aggregate figures above.
strengths: Owns the world's largest single-location aluminium smelter (Jharsuguda, 1.85 MTPA capacity) plus a captive alumina refinery at Lanjigarh (5 MTPA) - full backward integration
Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of ~48% (EBITDA ₹10,299 Cr on revenue ₹21,393 Cr), among the strongest in the domestic aluminium sector
Record Q2 FY27 production - aluminium output 649 KT (+5% YoY) and alumina output 895 KT (+37% YoY) - shows volumes still expanding
Already paid an ₹8/share interim dividend (record date 5 Aug 2026), giving a 2.15% trailing yield just months after listing
watchpoints: 99.99% of promoter group shares reported encumbered/pledged as of 18 Sep 2026 - a major ownership-risk flag so soon after listing
Stock down 23.7% from its June 2026 peak and has underperformed both the Nifty and peer Hindalco across every period measured since listing
Only one quarter of standalone financial results exists (Q1 FY27), and its YoY comparison uses carve-out/demerger-era figures rather than a clean like-for-like base
ROE, ROCE and net debt figures from public trackers are inconsistent/unreliable this early in the company's standalone life - genuine balance-sheet health is Not yet verifiable
Earnings are heavily tied to LME aluminium prices and alumina spreads, making margins cyclical rather than guaranteed
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 financial results (date not yet confirmed - check BSE/NSE filings, likely November 2026) will be the first quarter with a genuinely comparable standalone base and will show whether the 48% EBITDA margin holds; any update on the promoter pledge situation would be the other event that resolves the current ownership overhang.
analysis.data_notes: Price, return, dividend and drawdown figures are taken as given (verified) and not recomputed. Q1 FY27 results (revenue, EBITDA, PAT, EPS) and the 99.99% promoter pledge disclosure were cross-checked across the company's own press release and multiple independent market-news sources and are consistent. Q2 FY27 production figures are from the company's BSE filing/press coverage; Q2 financial results and the next results date could not be confirmed - flagged as Not verified. ROE, ROCE, and net debt figures shown by some data aggregators conflict with each other (0% ROE/ROCE alongside a reported net-cash position) and are likely artifacts of VAML's very short listed history; these are explicitly flagged as not independently verifiable rather than reported as fact.
